decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up lift and gradual downward wrist orientation on both sides; locating cameras, dolls and pens from current RGB.
Approach the two dolls in separate workspaces, orienting fingers downward. Plan dolls in blue basket; verify alignment before closing.
Lower to the dolls' bodies with small visual alignment corrections; close both grippers, then check retention by lifting.
Lift both dolls to verify retention; advance the left doll toward the blue basket while the right stays safely on its side.
RGB shows both dolls stayed on the table. Reopen, recenter over their bodies and approach lower for a second grasp.
Shift grasp toward the dolls' lower bodies to avoid the broad heads, close, then make a short retention-test lift.
Both dolls appear between the fingers. Lift clear, carry the left doll over the left half of blue basket, and hold the right doll back to avoid arm interference.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller increments, lowering the retained left doll into blue while the right arm waits.
Release the left doll inside blue, withdraw leftward, then start bringing the retained right doll toward the right half of blue.
The released left doll fell in front of blue, so it will need recovery. Carry right doll farther forward before release; approach a left-side camera without crossing arms.
Right doll has slipped before reaching blue. Reposition for a body grasp; close on the aligned left camera and make a small lift to verify retention.
Left camera appears retained; carry it toward white basket. Right fingers missed the doll; use head-view alignment to reposition over its body and retry gently.
Lower and release retained camera into white basket. Lift the right doll vertically before slowly carrying it toward blue, keeping the gripper fully closed.
Camera is visibly inside white. Right doll slipped again; defer it and approach the remaining left camera, moving the right arm away for clearance.
Align each gripper over a remaining camera, lower gently and close; test the left grasp with a short vertical lift.
Both cameras appear pinched. Lift them, transport the left one toward white, and stage the right one near the center-front for a safe sequential transfer.
Release the second camera farther inside white. Right camera was not retained; reopen, rotate to pinch its narrower dimension, and approach lower before retrying.
Corrected malformed row; no previous motion occurred. Advance right fingers over camera and lower before closing; approach fallen doll with left.
Lift the right camera to test retention and move it toward a center-front transfer spot. Align the left fingers lower around the doll's torso rather than the head.
Test the improved torso grasp by a slow vertical lift. Set the retained right camera down at center-front for sequential left-arm collection, then open right fingers.
The doll is not retained. Prioritize completing cameras: withdraw right arm from the staged camera and approach it with the left gripper angled into the center, without crossing arms.
Correct the rejected tensor from unchanged observation. Lower left onto the staged camera and test grasp; approach the right-side black pen.
Camera is centered between left fingers; lift and carry toward white. Correct right pen alignment forward and descend before closing.
Carry the third camera over white while keeping it closed. Lift the pinched black pen and begin moving it toward red, checking for visible retention.
Release third camera into white. Black pen remained on table; retry at a lower grasp height. Move left toward the other pen with its fingers aligned across the shaft.
Replan after continuity rejection. Close right fingers at the contact-limited height and test pen retention; lower left fingers onto the other pen's shaft and test a short lift.
Check pen retention with additional lift and gentle transport. Bring the right gripper over the red interior; keep the left pen grasp closed and clear of the table.
Neither pen followed the transport in head view. Reopen and approach lower; pull the right grasp back from the basket rim to avoid contact before closing.
Right fingers are obstructed by the basket rim: lift clear before retreating. Left fingers descend another few centimeters around the pen shaft, then close for a fresh test.
Recenter the left pen laterally, allow time for closure, then test lifting. Approach the right pen with a narrower opening to avoid striking the red basket's front rim.
Left pen is visibly lifted. Use blue for pens and red for dolls to avoid a pen handoff; carry left pen toward blue. Lower slightly and close right fingers around the black pen, then test retention.
Carry retained left pen over blue, accounting for its protruding end. Right pen is still on table; shift the right grasp outward along the shaft, reopen, descend and close again.
Use smaller increments after the continuity interruption to position the left pen fully over blue. Fine-adjust right fingers across the black pen, close, pause, and test a vertical lift.
Left forward reach is near an IK limit; tilt the wrist to move the pen farther over blue without extending the arm. Recenter the right pinch laterally onto the black shaft and retry.
Release the retained yellow-accented pen fully over blue, then clear the basket. Right pen still appears unretained; fine-align closer across its shaft and try a slightly lower pinch.
Yellow pen is visibly settled in blue. Test the right pen with a larger vertical lift while approaching the nearer doll's torso with left fingers at a lower height.
Center the left grip on the doll's torso and close lower. Retry the black pen with a narrow opening to clear the basket rim and a lower approach; check contact before transport.
Make a slow vertical retention test on both grips before any further transport; right approach was contact-limited near the basket.
The left doll may now be retained; move it back to verify and stage for the right arm. Clear the right wrist from the pen and reorient over the rim-adjacent doll, avoiding the basket wall.
Set the left-held doll at center-front and release for safe sequential collection. Lower the right gripper onto the other doll's torso, keeping fingers clear of the red rim, then close.
Right descent was contact-limited. Move the grasp toward the doll's legs and away from the basket wall before closing. Withdraw left arm from the staged doll to keep workspaces clear.
Fine-align the right grip onto the doll's torso using both views, lower below the torso top, close and pause before a small lift. Left remains clear.
Lift clear and rotate the right grip across the doll's narrow torso dimension instead of pinching along its body and head. Keep the left arm parked.
Continue the interrupted rotation with smaller increments, compensating the fingertip offset while descending over the doll's torso. Keep jaws partly open to clear the basket rim.
The right fingers now straddle the doll's torso. Descend slightly, close fully and pause, then test retention with a slow vertical lift.
Continue the right doll's vertical retention test, then begin a gentle motion toward the red basket while keeping the pinch closed.

The doll slipped leftward clear of the rim. Approach it with the left arm using the longer link-to-finger offset. Approach the black pen near its outer end, beyond the red basket wall, to avoid rim obstruction.
Use wrist-view centering: advance the left pinch onto the doll's torso. Align the right jaws perpendicular to the pen shaft and close after a small lateral and height correction; pause both grasps.
Shift left pinch down from the doll's face toward its torso. The right jaw is obstructed by the red rim; retreat with closed fingers to draw the pen away from that obstruction before retrying.

Right wrist remains obstructed: lift clear and switch to a vertical approach, removing the large forward fingertip offset. Make a small wrist-view correction to the left torso pinch and test it slowly.
Use the vertical wrist view to move the right pinch along the shaft and toward it laterally, with a narrow opening to clear the rim. Withdraw the empty left gripper for clearance.
Fine-align the right pinch using the pen's wrist-image displacement, descend and close. Reorient the left wrist vertically above the staged doll for a torso grasp.
Test the right pen pinch with a vertical lift. Lower the left vertical grip over the staged doll's torso using wrist-image alignment, keeping the left arm on its side.
Right pen was not lifted; maintain shaft alignment and descend lower with narrow jaws before closing. Shift left fingers from the doll's broad head to its narrower lower torso, then close.
Lift the left torso pinch slowly to verify retention. Fine-correct the right pinch a few millimeters onto the shaft, reclose, pause, then make a short lift test.

Left doll is visibly retained; rotate it over the center transfer area while staying left of center. Right pen remained on table, so descend another five centimeters with the now-vertical, narrowly opened grip before closing.

Lower the retained left doll at the center transfer spot after rotating its torso. Right descent is blocked by the red rim; move the wrist outside the basket edge and angle only the fingers back toward the pen's end.
Release the staged doll and withdraw the left arm. With the right wrist now outside the rim, lower the aligned fingers to the pen shaft, close, pause and make a small lift.
Pen remains on the table; descend farther now that the wrist clears the basket edge, with a small lateral correction before closing. Approach the other doll using the left vertical grip.
The black pen has visibly tilted at the pinch; test retention with a slow lift and withdrawal. Fine-align the left vertical grasp over the other doll's lower torso before closing.

Correct left alignment along the doll's body, close and test a small lift. The pen remains unretained; shift the right pinch laterally onto the shaft and descend below the previous contact height while the wrist stays outside the rim.

Both grips missed. Make small visual-servo corrections while open: move the left fingers toward the torso without crossing the arm, and lift/recenter the right jaws over the pen rather than continuing against the table.
Wrist views now show the torso and pen shaft near the pinch centers. Apply millimeter-scale corrections, close both grips with a pause, and perform short vertical retention tests.
Withdraw the empty left arm and leave the central dolls for a right-arm approach. Move the right pinch inward from the pen end, reclose at a lower height, then lift and draw it away from the basket.
Fine-align the shaft with the right jaw apex, close and pause, then lift and pull away from the rim. Park the left arm clear of the central work area.
The pen is still on the table. Reopen narrowly and approach lower with only the right arm; inspect the shaft between the open fingers before another closure.
At the contact-limited height, the shaft remains just outside the jaw gap. Shift the narrow right pinch eight millimeters laterally onto it, close and pause, then test a small lift.
The pen is still not retained and the rim prevents a full approach. Lift the closed right fingers to the empty red basket's front wall and gently try to move the basket back for clearance.
The basket did not visibly move. Switch to a more oblique approach from outside its right edge, keeping the wrist clear while lowering the fingers toward the pen's exposed end.
Replan from the tracking interruption: lift and retreat from the obstructing rim, then approach the unobstructed staged doll with a vertical right gripper. Leave the pen for a later approach.
Approach the unobstructed center-front doll with the right vertical gripper, keeping the link on the right side and the parked left arm clear. Inspect torso alignment before closing.
Center the right fingers across the staged doll's torso using wrist-image displacement, lower slightly, close and pause, then begin a short lift without crossing the arms.
Head view shows the right pinch still beside the doll. Reopen and angle the fingers toward its torso while keeping the right link on its side; inspect alignment before closing.
The unobstructed wrist view now shows the torso between the open jaws. Make a small centering adjustment, close and pause, then lift slowly to verify a body grasp.
The shallow pinch did not clearly retain the doll. Keep torso alignment, reopen and descend below the previous grasp height to engage the body sides, then close and pause.
The deeper right pinch now encloses the doll's body. Lift vertically and begin a gentle rightward transfer toward red, maintaining a closed grasp and checking retention.
